newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firms urge delay in MOF's tax plan for bonds.
newsitem.headline: Japan firms urge delay in MOF's tax plan for bonds.

text.p: Seventy one leading Japanese companies have jointly submitted a request to the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to maintain the current withholding tax exemption for foreigners for at least one more year, the firms said in a statement on Tuesday.

The group, which includes executives from giants such as Nippon Steel Corp, Tokyo Gas, Hitachi Ltd and Tokyo Electric Power Co, said the MOF's planned rule changes on Japanese bonds issued overseas, including Eurobonds, had a danger of hindering fundraising by Japanese borrowers.
"There should be a formal occasion for the MOF, issuers, investors, and foreign and domestic underwriters to get together to discuss the issue from various angles," the joint statement said.
It was the second time since October that the firms have jointly appealed to MOF about the plan.
The companies also said there was a need to keep the impact of the rule as small as possible to the market and to come up with a way that could be widely be accepted by market participants.
"For Japanese firms, the Eurobond market is indispensable," it said. "The competitiveness of Eurobonds issued by Japanese firms could suffer greatly."

The MOF plan, disclosed last week, is aimed at closing a tax loophole in foreign bond investment by requiring foreigners to identify themselves in order to be exempt from paying the withholding tax for such investments.

Meanwhile, in a separate letter to MOF's International Tax Division, the Swiss Bankers Association said Swiss-domiciled banks and the Swiss clearing system are neither able nor allowed to provide any kind of information or certification, which the MOF requires for the plan.
Since the MOF first said it did not intend to keep the current tax exemption law as it is, there have been appeals from various industries.

Shortly after the MOF disclosed its plan last week, Goldman Sachs, Merrill Lynch, Salomon Brothers and SBC Warburg also submitted a petition suggesting the ministry needed to conduct a thorough study before finalising the plan.
MOF has already submitted the plan to the ruling Liberal Democratic Party's tax panel.
Industry sources said they expect the panel's decision sometime next week.
